subject: ordinal,relation_type
justification: ordinal is a positional bookkeeping index inside one page's parse (builder lines 488, 500) and relation_type has 3 values; neither identifies anything. The FD holds only because every page on this site emits the same templated head, so the nth resource reference is the same tag on all 422 pages. One page with an extra stylesheet breaks it.

subject: source_stable_id,target_stable_id -> text
justification: the directed reference from one mirrored page to one target resource (source page x target resource) owns text. edges.text is built as '{source_url} {relation_type} {target_url}' (builder line 673), and (source, target) fixes relation_type structurally: link/page/asset stable ids live in disjoint hash namespaces and references_asset vs references_svg is decided by the target itself (builder lines 572, 614, 632; measured 0 of 16636 pairs carry two relation types). So the source-to-target reference genuinely owns this derived label. The pair is not one of the packet's intended_keys, which makes this a load-bearing redundancy: text should be derived, not stored.

subject: source_stable_id,target_url -> text
justification: the directed reference from one mirrored page to one target resource, with the target named by URL owns text. Same construction invariant: text = '{source_url} {relation_type} {target_url}' (builder line 673) and the pair fixes relation_type (0 of 16636 pairs carry two). Stable id and URL are interchangeable on both sides - ids are deterministic hashes of the URL (builder lines 150-159), measured 422 source ids to 422 source urls and 1396 target ids to 1396 target urls.

subject: source_url,target_stable_id -> text
justification: the directed reference from one mirrored page to one target resource, with the source named by URL owns text. Same construction invariant as the id/id form: text is the formatted concatenation of source_url, relation_type and target_url (builder line 673), and relation_type is fixed by the pair. The URL/id substitution is safe because page and asset ids are deterministic hashes of the URL (builder lines 150-159).

subject: source_url,target_url -> text
justification: the directed reference from one mirrored page to one target resource (both named by URL) owns text. The most direct form of the same fact: text literally is source_url + relation_type + target_url (builder line 673), with relation_type determined by the target's namespace and kind (builder lines 572, 614, 632). Real at any row count, and again not a declared key - the label is stored redundantly.

subject: tag
justification: The builder explicitly permits several attributes per tag - ASSET_ATTRS maps img to ('src','srcset'), video to ('src','poster'), use to ('href','xlink:href'), plus synthesised 'style:url' and 'url' attrs (builder lines 46-56, 240, 457). The FD holds only because this mirror happens to use src on img/script and href on link and nothing else (measured 4 tags, 3 attrs, one attr per tag). A single srcset or inline style breaks it; an HTML tag does not own the attribute a page referenced it through.

subject: target_stable_id -> attr
justification: attr and tag describe the element that carries the link -- href/link, src/img, src/script -- so they are properties of the edge, not of the target it points at. Across 17422 edges over 1396 targets each target happens to be referenced the same way, which a single page linking one URL both as an anchor and as an image would end.

subject: target_stable_id -> tag
justification: attr and tag describe the element that carries the link -- href/link, src/img, src/script -- so they are properties of the edge, not of the target it points at. Across 17422 edges over 1396 targets each target happens to be referenced the same way, which a single page linking one URL both as an anchor and as an image would end.

subject: target_stable_id -> target_url
justification: the target resource (page, off-site link, or asset) identified by its stable id owns target_url. target_stable_id is a deterministic hash of the target URL (builder lines 150-159, 540, 578), so the target resource owns its URL - measured 1396 ids to 1396 urls, 0 violations in either direction. attr and tag are NOT owned: they record how one particular referring page spelled the reference, and nothing in the model stops the same file being reached as from one page and via CSS url() from another (builder lines 46-56, 240). They ride along only because this mirror is uniform.

subject: target_url -> attr
justification: target_url and target_stable_id identify the same thing, so this is the previous ruling under another name: attr and tag describe the element carrying the link, not the target it points at.

subject: target_url -> tag
justification: target_url and target_stable_id identify the same thing, so this is the previous ruling under another name: attr and tag describe the element carrying the link, not the target it points at.

subject: target_url -> target_stable_id
justification: the target resource identified by its URL owns target_stable_id. The inverse of the same identity map: the stable id is computed from netloc+path+query of the URL (builder lines 146-159, 578), so the target resource owns its id (0 violations over 17422 rows). attr and tag are excluded for the same reason as under target_stable_id - they are per-reference markup facts of the referring page, not attributes of the target.

subject: text
justification: The pair owns the derived label; the label does not own its components. text is the formatted concatenation written at builder line 673, so it re-yields target_url only by string containment with the direction of derivation reversed, and it is near-unique (16636 distinct over 17422 rows). tag and attr ride on exactly the target->tag coincidence rejected under target_stable_id. Treating this as real would license normalising edges around its own display string.

subject: model
value: One row is one individual reference occurrence: the n-th outgoing reference of a given relation type on one crawled page, pointing at one link or asset target.
justification: `_edge_row` (662-688) is called once per ref (573, 633), so a row is one reference occurrence, and its `stable_id` (declared PRIMARY KEY, 414) is hashed from `{source}:{relation_type}:{target}:{ordinal}` (671). `ordinal` is `enumerate(parser.links)` for links_to and `enumerate(parser.resources)` for references_asset/references_svg (488-512): two disjoint index spaces, each index producing exactly one row, with relation_type separating the spaces. Hence (source, relation_type, ordinal) identifies a row by construction and determines the target — verified: 0 collisions over 17,422 rows, while (source, ordinal) alone collides 6,837 times, exactly as the two enumerations predict. `source_url` and `source_stable_id` are bijective via `_page_stable_id` (150-155; 422/422 distinct page urls), so both spellings are the same key. The other nine observed combinations are artifacts: `attr` and `tag` are '' on every links_to edge (681-683); the target_stable_id/target_url variants drop relation_type and survive only because link ids and asset ids never share a subdomain prefix; `ordinal,text` rides on text = source_url+relation_type+target_url (673). Scope per-build (405-407).

Hence (source, relation_type, ordinal) identifies a row by construction and determines the target — verified: 0 collisions over 17,422 rows, while (source, ordinal) alone collides 6,837 times, exactly as the two enumerations predict. `source_url` and `source_stable_id` are bijective via `_page_stable_id` (150-155; 422/422 distinct page urls), so both spellings are the same key. The other nine observed combinations are artifacts: `attr` and `tag` are '' on every links_to edge (681-683); the target_stable_id/target_url variants drop relation_type and survive only because link ids and asset ids never share a subdomain prefix; `ordinal,text` rides on text = source_url+relation_type+target_url (673). Scope per-build (405-407).

subject: disposition
justification: 7 adjudicated dependency(ies) violate 3NF under the approved keys: sha256 -> asset_ref_count; sha256 -> bytes; sha256 -> headings_json; sha256 -> outgoing_link_count (and 3 more). Nothing regenerates this database -- it has no builder and is its own source of truth -- so unlike the generated catalogues the update anomalies are real and the redundancy can drift. Fixing it means migrating the file in place with a lossless proof and a compatibility view, which has not been done. This is the exemption most worth revisiting. Its document-valued columns (headings_json) were separately accepted and are not what blocks it.

subject: asset_ref_count,headings_json
justification: headings_json is a near-unique JSON blob (403 distinct over 422 rows) and asset_ref_count is a 23-value tally. A page's heading text owns neither the number of resources it references nor the number of links it emits - both are lengths of parse lists (builder lines 480-481).

subject: asset_ref_count,title
justification: A 23-value count plus a near-unique title (402 distinct over 422 rows). The title is the <title> text; it does not own the heading list, the link tally, or the URL-derived section (builder lines 130-133, 470-481).

subject: bytes
justification: The textbook coincidence: a file size determining a section. bytes is a byte count with 381 distinct values, section is the first path segment of the URL (builder lines 130-133, 470). The 31 size collisions merely happen to fall inside one section each.

subject: bytes,headings_json
justification: Two near-unique columns at once (381 and 403 distinct over 422 rows). sha256 and text are content facts of the file and the two counts are parse-list lengths (builder lines 339, 460-481); a size plus a heading list owns none of them.

subject: bytes,outgoing_link_count
justification: A near-unique byte count (381 distinct) plus a 36-value tally determining another tally. Both counts are lengths of independent parse lists (builder lines 480-481) with no dependency between them; they simply do not collide across 422 rows.

subject: bytes,title
justification: A near-unique size (381 distinct) plus a near-unique title (402 distinct). The real content determinant for sha256/text/headings is the file content, keyed by sha256 - this pair is a coincidental stand-in for it, and it drags in counts the title cannot own.

subject: headings_json
justification: A near-unique JSON column (403 distinct over 422 rows, a single duplicate group of 20 stub pages). It appears to determine title only because this site's stubs repeat one heading set, and section is URL-derived (builder lines 130-133); heading text owns neither.

subject: headings_json,outgoing_link_count
justification: Carried by the near-unique headings JSON (403 distinct). asset_ref_count is len(parser.resources) (builder line 481) - a property of the page's markup, not of its headings or its link tally.

subject: outgoing_link_count,title
justification: A 36-value tally plus a near-unique title (402 distinct). The title does not own the heading list, the resource tally, or the URL-derived section (builder lines 130-133, 470-481).

subject: section,title
justification: section has 3 values and title is near-unique (402 distinct over 422 rows), so the title alone very nearly settles the row; section only patches the one repeated stub title. A page's title does not own its heading list.

subject: sha256 -> bytes,headings_json,title,text,asset_ref_count,outgoing_link_count
justification: the mirrored page file content (the digest is that content's identity; the relation's key stays url/stable_id) owns bytes, headings_json, title, text, asset_ref_count, outgoing_link_count. The one determinant here that survives inspection, and it is not vacuous: sha256 has two genuine duplicate groups (420 distinct over 422 rows - person/dan-rust vs person/james-j-walton, and person/c-godreche vs person/l-billard), and within each group every content-derived attribute agrees because the builder parses all of them out of the same bytes it digested (builder lines 339, 451-486). section is excluded: it is derived from the URL path (builder lines 130-133, 470) and agrees here only because both duplicate pairs happen to be /person/ pages - two byte-identical stubs in different sections would break it. Caveat on bytes: it comes from the manifest record with file size as fallback (builder lines 335-338), so it is content-determined in practice rather than by construction.

subject: text
justification: The near-unique free-text column, 420 distinct over 422 rows - the same two duplicate groups sha256 has. Unlike the digest, this projection is lossy by construction: markup-stripped, script-free normalised text (builder lines 262-276, 355-376), so different files can share it and it cannot own bytes, sha256 or the resource/link tallies. Where it does echo title and headings it is only re-reading its own concatenation with the direction of derivation reversed; section is URL-derived. The label does not own its components.

subject: model
value: One row is one mirrored HTML page from the three target sections (substitution/person/glossary) of the Bielefeld Tilings Encyclopedia site walk, with its parsed metadata, file digest and extracted text.
justification: The packet carried builder_path=null; I resolved the authority by grepping for `bielefeld_tiling_page`, and confirmed it because the parsed manifest's source_root matches DEFAULT_SOURCE_ROOT (27-35) and sample relative_path matches `str(local_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT))` (329-331). `_write_sqlite` (404-430) unlinks and recreates catalog.sqlite each run and declares `stable_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` on every table (414); SQLite's unique index would abort the executemany, so stable_id uniqueness is build-enforced. A page row is emitted once per mirror record that is HTML and a target-section URL (448-487); `stable_id = _page_stable_id(url)` is a pure function of netloc+path+query (150-155), `page_by_url` (527) treats url as identity, and the dlt contract uses id_fallback_keys=("stable_id","url") (dlt:29). Verified 422/422 distinct urls. `local_path`/`relative_path` are only where the fetcher stored the copy (329-331, 476-477); two URLs can land on one file, so their observed uniqueness is a mirror-layout artifact, not identity. Scope is per-build: sha256/bytes/local_path describe the mirror at parse time and the whole file is rewritten each run (405-407).

subject: model
value: One row is one SVG graphic in the walk: either one inline <svg> occurrence inside a crawled page, or one external .svg asset referenced by the pages.
justification: `svgs` is a union of two branches. Inline (513-525): one row per `<svg` occurrence, with `url = record.url` and page_url/page_stable_id set, so N inline SVGs on one page share url, page_url and page_stable_id and carry no local_path, relative_path, sha256 or asset_stable_id.
